stand.question: Where can I buy a stand?
stand.answer: You can buy a stand for £12.99 at <stand>https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B07NVBXYPJ</stand>.

videos.question: Are there video guides?
videos.answer: Yes. The "How to use ChessCam" playlist on YouTube has a short video for each mode. Open it with Video guides in the menu at the top right.

camera.question: How do I set up my camera?
camera.step1: Put your phone or camera on a stand to the side of the board, in landscape.
camera.step2: Make sure that the stand is stable and that the camera can see the whole board.
camera.step3: Make sure that the tallest piece (the king or queen) is still in shot when placed on the furthest square from the camera.
camera.step4: If the board is small in the shot, click Draw Region and drag a box around it.
camera.step5: ChessCam zooms the camera out as far as it can. To use a different camera, choose it from the Device menu.

moving.question: Will the app work if the board or the camera move mid-way through?
moving.answer: Yes, as long as the whole board stays inside the region. If you have not drawn a region, the whole board must stay in shot.

power.question: How powerful does my device have to be?
power.answer: The app needs to run at least 1 FPS. The speed is shown in the top right corner of the video.

record.question: How do I record?
record.step1: Click Record on the Home page, or go straight to https://www.chesscam.net/record.
record.step2: Set up your camera (see "How do I set up my camera?").
record.step3: Press the red record button over the video, or press K, to start recording. Press it again to pause.
record.reset: To start again from the beginning, press the eraser button over the video. If the game has moves, press it a second time to confirm.

upload.question: How do I upload a game?
upload.step1: Click Upload on the Home page, or go straight to https://www.chesscam.net/upload.
upload.step2: Click Choose Video and pick a video of the game. MP4 (H.264/AAC) and WebM files work in most browsers.
upload.step3: If the board is small in the video, click Draw Region and drag a box around it.
upload.step4: Press the play button over the video, or press K, to start detecting moves.
upload.speed: The speed button over the video switches between 1x, 2x and 4x. 1x is the most accurate.
upload.seek: Use the seek bar or the arrow keys to skip through the video. Skipping pauses the video, so you can check the board before going on. The eraser button resets the game to the start position.
upload.eval: The bar beside the video shows Stockfish's evaluation of the position. It's on when you open Upload, and off when you open Record or Broadcast, as the players at the board could see it. Switch it with Engine evaluation in the menu at the top right. It never shows when playing on Lichess.

play.question: How do I play a Lichess game on a real board?
play.step2: Click Play on the Home page, or go straight to https://www.chesscam.net/play. Sign in with Lichess if you are asked to.
play.step3: Set up your camera (see "How do I set up my camera?").
play.step4: Choose your game from Select a Game.
play.step5: Press the play button over the video, or press K, to start detecting moves.
play.moves: The moves you make on your board are sent to Lichess. Your opponent's moves are shown on the board in the sidebar, so you can play them on your board.
play.limits: Lichess only allows this for Rapid, Classical and Correspondence games.

broadcast.question: How do I broadcast a game to Lichess?
broadcast.step1: Create a broadcast on the Lichess website, if you don't have one already.
broadcast.step2: Click Broadcast on the Home page, or go straight to https://www.chesscam.net/broadcast. Sign in with Lichess if you are asked to.
broadcast.step3: Set up your camera (see "How do I set up my camera?").
broadcast.step4: Choose the broadcast round from Select a Study. Only rounds that you can edit are listed.
broadcast.step5: Choose the board number, from 1 to 64, from Select a Board.
broadcast.step6: Press the red record button over the video, or press K, to start broadcasting.
broadcast.moves: Each move is sent to the broadcast as it is detected, with the whole game so far. If sending fails because of a connection problem, an error shows at the top of the screen, and the next move fills in what was missed. Nothing is sent again until then, so if the last move of the game fails to send, check the broadcast on Lichess.

position.question: Can I start from a custom position?
position.intro: Yes, when recording or uploading. Before starting, set up the position on your board, then choose an option from the Position menu:
position.white: Detect (White to move): reads the position from the camera, with White to move.
position.black: Detect (Black to move): reads the position from the camera, with Black to move.
position.check: Check the board in the sidebar after detecting, as a misread piece will stop later moves from being recognised.

corners.question: What are the labels in the corners of the video?
corners.answer: While the app is detecting moves, it labels each corner of the region (or of the whole video, if you have not drawn a region) with the square it thinks is there: a1, a8, h1 or h8. If the labels are wrong, moves will be misread. This is most likely when the board is at about 45 degrees to the camera, so turn the board or the camera until its edges are closer to the edges of the video.

save.question: How do I save my game?
save.answer: Click Copy PGN in the sidebar to copy the game to the clipboard. Recorded games include the time each move took, from when it was seen, to about a second. Time spent paused is not counted.

export.question: How do I send my game to Lichess?
export.intro: After recording or uploading a game, click Lichess in the sidebar, next to Copy PGN:
export.open: Open in Lichess imports the game to Lichess and opens it in a new tab. You don't need to sign in.
export.study: Add to a study saves the game to one of your Lichess studies, named after the current date and time. Sign in with Lichess from the menu first. If no studies are listed, create one on the Lichess website.
export.signIn: Signing in leaves the page, so a game in progress is lost. Copy the PGN first to keep it.

offline.question: Does the app work offline?
offline.answer: Once you have used Record or Upload with an internet connection, they also work offline. Playing, broadcasting and sending games to Lichess need a connection, but you can still copy the PGN.

illegal.question: How are illegal moves handled?
illegal.answer: Illegal moves are ignored by the app.

privacy.question: Are my videos kept private?
privacy.answer: Yes. Uploaded videos and the camera feed are processed on your device. ChessCam never receives them.

licences.question: What licences cover the board recognition model?
licences.answer: The model is a ChessQueries model with a MobileNetV4 encoder, published on <hf>Hugging Face</hf>. Its weights are available under the <polyform>PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0</polyform>. See the <notice>NOTICE</notice> for details.

openSource.question: Is ChessCam open source?
openSource.answer: Yes. The code is on <github>GitHub</github>, under the AGPL-3.0 licence, and the board recognition model is on <hf>Hugging Face</hf>. You can report bugs and suggest ideas on GitHub too.

contact.question: How can I get in touch?
contact.happy: I am always happy to chat about any ideas or problems that you might have!
